planting.note: Direct-sow after soil has warmed and frost danger has passed, since this bush bean has no cold tolerance.

directions: BRS Pérola was released by EMBRAPA Arroz e Feijão in the mid-1990s and quickly became one of the most widely grown carioca-type common beans in Brazil, prized for its light beige, lightly streaked seed coat that meets commercial grain standards. Plants have a semi-erect growth habit with a roughly 85-to-95-day cycle from sowing to physiological maturity and white flowers. It carries resistance to rust and common mosaic virus plus one anthracnose race, with intermediate resistance to fusarium wilt and angular leaf spot, making it a relatively low-input garden bean. Grow as a direct-sown bush bean in full sun with even moisture during flowering and pod fill for best yield.
sources: EMBRAPA Arroz e Feijão — Feijão Pérola cultivar record

planting.note: Direct-sow once soil is warm and settled since this upright bean was bred for mechanized harvest and has no frost tolerance.

directions: BRS Estilo is a carioca-type common bean released by EMBRAPA in 2009, bred for an erect plant architecture that resists lodging and suits direct mechanical harvest while keeping grains close in size and appearance to the earlier BRS Pérola. It has a normal 85-to-90-day cycle from emergence to physiological maturity, resistance to eight anthracnose pathotypes and common mosaic virus, and moderate resistance to rust, with seeds reported to cook in about 26 minutes. It is recommended across a dozen Brazilian states from Rio Grande do Sul to Pernambuco. In the garden, grow it as a bush bean in full sun with consistent watering through pod fill.
sources: EMBRAPA — BRS Estilo cultivar technical bulletin (Comunicado Técnico 169)

planting.note: Plant stem cuttings after all frost danger has passed into warm, well-drained soil, since cassava is killed by cold.

directions: BRS Kiriris is an industrial cassava cultivar released by EMBRAPA Mandioca e Fruticultura in 2001, selected for the starch- and flour-processing regions of Bahia's Valença, Jequié, and Santo Antônio de Jesus micro-regions. It yields around 30% starch content and shows marked resistance to root rot along with broad adaptability, which has made it a mainstay on Brazilian starch-processing farms. Propagate from mature, disease-free stem cuttings planted horizontally or at an angle in warm, well-drained soil, and expect a long single harvest cycle of roughly 10 to 14 months for best root yield. Keep plantings weed-free during establishment but reduce watering once the canopy closes, since cassava tolerates drought well.
sources: EMBRAPA Mandioca e Fruticultura — Mandioca BRS Kiriris cultivar record

planting.note: Plant stem cuttings in warm soil after frost risk has passed; this cultivar tolerates dry spells once established.

directions: BRS Formosa was released by EMBRAPA Mandioca e Fruticultura in 2003, bred with participation from EMBRAPA Cerrados specifically for bacterial-blight resistance and drought tolerance so it could succeed in the semi-arid Caatinga climate of Northeast Brazil. It is grown for industrial flour and starch production and performs best in root yield and dry-matter content when harvested after a single cycle rather than two. Start from healthy stem cuttings planted in well-drained soil during the warm season, and expect minimal irrigation needs once the plants are established thanks to its drought hardiness. This makes it a good choice for hot, low-rainfall garden sites where other cassava cultivars would struggle.
sources: EMBRAPA Mandioca e Fruticultura — Mandioca BRS Formosa cultivar record

planting.note: Start seedlings or grafted plants well ahead of the warm season and transplant only after all frost danger has passed, since this vine has no cold tolerance.

directions: BRS Gigante Amarelo (registered as BRS GA1) is a yellow sour passion fruit cultivar released by EMBRAPA in 2008 and bred for high productivity and fresh-market and processing quality; it has become one of the most widely planted passion fruit cultivars in Brazil. Fruits are oblong, yellow, and typically weigh 120 to 350 grams with roughly 40% pulp yield, though early-season fruit can exceed 500 grams. Train the vigorous vines on a sturdy trellis in full sun with spacing around 2.5 by 2.5 meters, and irrigate during dry periods since irrigated plantings have reached about 42 tonnes per hectare in the first year. It adapts to most frost-free regions and soil types but will not tolerate freezing temperatures.
sources: EMBRAPA — Maracujá BRS Gigante Amarelo (BRS GA1) cultivar record

planting.note: Start plants ahead of season and set out only once frost risk is over; this cultivar is not recommended for frost-prone gardens.

directions: BRS Rubi do Cerrado (BRS RC) was released by EMBRAPA in 2012 after breeding through population improvement, recurrent selection, and evaluation of inter- and intraspecific hybrids. It stands out among passion fruit cultivars for greater tolerance of airborne diseases such as viral infections and bacteriosis, along with anthracnose and verrucosis resistance, plus better post-harvest shelf life and transport durability. Grow it on a strong trellis in full sun with regular watering during fruit set; well-managed plantings in the Federal District, Rio de Janeiro, and Mato Grosso have exceeded 50 tonnes per hectare in the first production year. It adapts to nearly all frost-free regions of Brazil but should not be planted where freezes occur.
sources: EMBRAPA — Maracujá BRS Rubi do Cerrado (BRS RC) cultivar record

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost and transplant once nights stay warm, since this open-pollinated serrano has no cold tolerance.

directions: CHISER-522 is an open-pollinated slender serrano pepper released by INIFAP in 2019 as the institute's first thin-type serrano variety, bred for disease tolerance and improved yield for growers in southern Tamaulipas, northern and Los Tuxtlas Veracruz, and eastern San Luis Potosí. Vigorous plants reach 90 to 130 centimeters tall with an intermediate cycle of about 80 days to flowering and 110 days to first harvest, bearing slim fruit. It shows tolerance to bacterial leaf spot and powdery mildew and under drip irrigation can yield about 50% more than local criollo varieties. Grow in full sun with consistent moisture and support stems if fruit load is heavy on the compact plants.
sources: INIFAP / Secretaría de Agricultura — Primera variedad de chile serrano delgado CHISER-522

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost, since habanero-type peppers are slow to germinate and need a long warm season to fruit well.

directions: Calakmul is a free-pollinated habanero pepper variety developed by INIFAP and introduced around 2016 to give Yucatán and Campeche growers a cultivar with tolerance to viral disease, which in trials showed substantially lower infection rates than standard commercial habanero stock. Fruits ripen from light green to red, measuring roughly 5 centimeters long and 3.5 centimeters across with an average weight near 15 grams, and the cultivar is mainly grown for sauce and salsa processing. Open-field yields run 28 to 30 tonnes per hectare, rising above 32 tonnes under protected structures. Grow in full sun with warm, humid conditions and consistent watering, and expect the characteristically intense heat typical of habanero-type Capsicum chinense.
sources: INIFAP — Genera INIFAP nueva variedad de chile habanero Calakmul

planting.note: Start seed indoors 4-6 weeks before the last frost and transplant once soil has warmed, as this cultivar has no frost tolerance.

directions: INI-181 is a husk tomato (tomatillo) variety developed by INIFAP for the El Bajío growing region of Guanajuato through stratified mass selection and individual plant selection, and it is registered in Mexico's National Catalog of Plant Varieties. Plants are semi-erect with long, non-pigmented internodes, hairless stems, and elliptical green leaves with toothed margins. Fruit is firm and green, held tightly by the papery calyx with a shallow stem cavity, and the variety shows tolerance to powdery mildew and to the tomatillo stem borer. Basic seed stock is maintained at the INIFAP Bajío Experimental Field in Celaya; grow in full sun with consistent moisture and space plants generously since mature vines sprawl widely.
sources: INIFAP — INI-181: nueva variedad de tomate de cáscara para El Bajío, Revista Mexicana de Ciencias Agrícolas
